exposure: reasons for preferring vaginal birth (easier post-partum recovery, personal desire)
reasons for preferring cesarean section (fear of labor pain, personal desire)
outcome: maternal preference for type of delivery in early pregnancy
cohort: The study included 655 postpartum women recruited from a low-risk maternity hospital in Lagarto, Sergipe, Brazil.
finding: The primary finding was that 73.3% of women preferred a vaginal birth mainly due to easier post-partum recovery or personal desire, while those preferring a cesarean section (n=142) cited fear of labor pain and personal desire as main reasons, and initial preference impacted the final delivery route.
mod_finding: Mothers' initial preference for type of birth in early pregnancy showed a greater frequency of occurrence for the desired type of birth (PR: 2.07) and had an impact on the final route of delivery.
